title: Breaking Information Cocoons: A Hyperbolic Framework for Balancing Exploration and Exploitation in Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Recommender systems need to balance content exploration and exploitation while allowing users to adjust recommendation preferences.

gap.claim: Existing approaches struggle to represent hierarchical structures, lack semantic understanding of user and item profiles, and do not provide a principled mechanism for balancing exploration and exploitation.

contributions.claim: HERec is a hyperbolic framework for balancing exploration and exploitation in recommender systems.
The framework aligns textual descriptions with collaborative information directly in hyperbolic space through a semantic-enhanced hierarchical mechanism.

The framework uses automatic hierarchical clustering based on optimizing Dasgupta's cost to discover hierarchical structures without predefined hyperparameters and enable user-adjustable exploration-exploitation trade-offs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that theoretical gradient analysis shows the alignment leverages the hyperbolic manifold structure and improves modeling of users and items.
The authors report that extensive experiments show HERec outperforms Euclidean and hyperbolic baselines, with up to 5.49% improvement in utility metrics and 11.39% increase in diversity metrics.
The authors report that HERec effectively mitigates information cocoons.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommender systems can restrict exposure to diverse content and create information cocoons.
The task is to balance exploration and exploitation while supporting user-adjustable preferences.
Existing Euclidean and hyperbolic approaches have limitations in hierarchical representation, semantic understanding, and principled trade-off control.
HERec combines semantic-enhanced hyperbolic alignment with automatic hierarchical clustering.
The authors report theoretical analysis and experiments showing improved utility, diversity, and mitigation of information cocoons.

source_observation.claim: HERec aligns textual descriptions with collaborative information in hyperbolic space and reports gains in both utility and diversity metrics.

interpretation.claim: Combining semantic and collaborative signals may help address the trade-off between recommendation relevance and content diversity.

application.claim: Multi-signal recommender designs can evaluate utility and diversity together when targeting reduced information cocoons.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the datasets, metric definitions, statistical significance, or conditions under which the reported improvements hold.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, experimental protocols, or baseline implementations.
The abstract does not define the utility and diversity metrics or report statistical significance.
The abstract does not provide details of the theoretical gradient analysis or clustering optimization.
The abstract does not establish generalization beyond the reported experiments.
